summary: Card opened directly in doing (in-progress). FIX for the Krea2 upscale op, which produced heavy noise - unusable on raw (turbo OFF) and only passable on turbo, because the accelerator (turbo distill) LoRA was applied in BOTH tiers. User reauthored the raw template (34 -> 38 nodes): new MpiIfElse 'is high tier' driven off the existing Input_Tier via MpiMath 'a == 1' now picks the UltimateSDUpscale model, so tier 1 runs the base model with no accelerator LoRA; and a refiner chain (VAEEncode -> ClownsharKSampler_Beta -> VAEDecode) was appended between the upscale and Output_image. The refiner deliberately runs on the accelerator-LoRA model in both tiers as a cheap 2-step polish - user-confirmed intentional. Blast radius verified zero: the moved node ids are unreferenced in js/ and routes/, injection is title-keyed, Output_image is unchanged, krea2Turbo already ships Input_Tier on the upscale command, upscalers are deliberately excluded from progressStages, and no new node types were introduced. Detail in brief.md.

Refiner exposed a progress defect - FIXED in js/services/phaseProgress.js. progressStages.js was NOT the mechanism: phaseProgress.tile() overrides the total with the live tile count when UltimateSDUpscale's outer bar reports, so a static entry would be discarded on the first tile. Real bug was that tile mode was one-way - once _tileMode was set, step() only moved _percent and never advanced _stage, so the refiner's bar was swallowed and the fill ran 0-100 percent a second time while the readout sat on the last tile (reads as a stall at the end of every upscale). Rejected the simpler '_total = tiles + 1': it fixes the printed total but not the stall, and tile() is shared by all 9 USDU cards - the 7 without a refiner would advertise a stage that never runs. Fix counts inner bars since the last tile bar; USDU emits its tile bar before every tile's inner bar, so during tiling the counter resets each tile and only a post-tile pass reaches 2. On the second bar it leaves tile mode and falls through to the normal per-bar logic, which stages it and self-corrects the total. 1 tile -> 2/2, 4 tiles -> 5/5. tile() untouched, so tile counting is unchanged. Ceiling named in the comment: assumes one inner bar per tile, true while all 9 USDU cards run seam_fix_mode None (swept). Guarded by tests/tile-post-pass-stage.test.cjs, 5 cases, negative-control proven (3 of 5 fail against the unfixed module, 5/5 pass restored). eslint clean. Still NOT verified in the app.

Live app test caught a hole in the first progress fix. routes/comfy.js forwards the RAW tqdm value from 'USDU: t/T', so T tiles emit T+1 events (0/T .. T/T) - the last fires AFTER the final tile's inner bar. The first cut re-armed the post-tile detector on EVERY tile bar, so that trailing tick re-armed it after the last tile and the refiner never tripped it; app still read 1/1 on both stages. Guard is now 'if (tileIndex < tiles)' - arm only for a tile that will actually run. The original test called tile() once per tile and never modelled the trailing tick, so it passed against broken code: a WRONG test, not a thin one. It now models the tick explicitly. Also added the user's requested honest total: progressStages.js records 'krea2_upscaler.json': {postTile: 1} (no 'single' - the tile count is a runtime value that tile mode overrides), new postTileBarsFor() shares _baseKey with stagesFor, commandExecutor passes it into createStageProgress, and tile() uses _total = _tileOffset + tiles + _postTileBars. A blanket +1 in tile() was rejected because 7 of the 9 USDU cards have no refiner and would advertise a stage that never runs. Stage clamp in tile() also had to move from min(_total, ...) to min(_tileOffset + tiles, ...) or the trailing tick advances into the refiner slot early. Now: grid off 1/2 -> 2/2; grid on 4 tiles 1/5..4/5 -> 5/5; other upscalers unchanged. Test at 6 cases, all pass; TWO negative controls - vs unfixed HEAD 5 of 6 fail, vs the first cut 4 of 6 fail including both trailing-tick cases. eslint clean on all three touched modules. Verified: postTileBarsFor returns 1 for both krea2 upscaler variants and 0 for chroma/sdxl/pony/ill, stagesFor unregressed (krea2_t2i 2, ltx_t2v 3). Awaiting user re-test in the app.

USER-VERIFIED LIVE, both halves. Progress: grid off read 1/2 during the tile then 2/2 on the refiner; grid on with 2 tiles read 2/3 then 3/3 (load bar does not register as a stage, so _tileOffset is 0 - 2 tiles + 1 refiner = 3). The earlier '9/9 twice' report was NOT a defect: that run had total_tiles=8 per logs/app.log, so 8 tiles + refiner = 9, and the two 9/9 sightings were the refiner's two steps (0/2 at 0:59, 1/2 at 1:17, matching log timestamps 21:51:23 and 21:51:38). It reads like a stall because the refiner is 2 steps at ~15s each on the full frame. That exact logged sequence is now replayed as a test case. Upscale quality also confirmed by the user: refiner makes raw usable and turbo much better. Suite tests/tile-post-pass-stage.test.cjs 7/7; negative controls 5/6 fail vs unfixed HEAD and 5/7 fail vs the first cut. Touched: js/services/phaseProgress.js, js/data/progressStages.js, js/services/commandExecutor.js, plus the synced workflow cards. Generated workflow files remain STAGED for mpi-end to commit.

TIER-1 BRANCH NOW VERIFIED LIVE - both sides of the MpiIfElse gate confirmed. Non-turbo upscale of t2i_038 (768x1344) produced upscale_018 at 1152x2016 (correct 1.5x) with stages 1/3 -> 2/3 -> 3/3 (2 tiles + refiner). This is the first run to take the 'is high tier' TRUE path: Input_Tier 1 -> MpiMath 'a == 1' true -> node 1685 FromBasicPipe base model, no accelerator LoRA on the UltimateSDUpscale tiles, refiner still distilled. Every earlier upscale sidecar recorded Input_Tier 2, so only the false path had been exercised until now. Tile stages were visibly slower than the turbo runs while the refiner stage stayed quick - the expected asymmetry of the gate. User also ran a side-by-side compare of upscale_017 (turbo) vs upscale_018 (non-turbo) and accepted both. Card was already done/complete; this closes the last unexercised path in the template rewire.
